tone_statements.quote: e) The principles of marking tones using diacritics in Tarok need to be stated out. These are for high, for low, ̂ for falling, ̌ for rising and unmarked for mid. [...] lexical tones can be marked and grammatical tones should be marked in full. [...] In Tarok, the dative construction is marked in 2 ways: through the particle a meaning „to /for‟ and a falling tone on the noun or pronoun prefixes. [...] 16. Tone marking The rule of thumb is for all grammatical tones to be marked fully but lexical tones very sparingly. In academic writings the tone for every Tarok word or particle must be marked.
tone_statements.locator: items 4(e), 8 'Writing the dative construction', 12 'Writing vocative constructions', 16 'Tone marking'
tone_statements.summary: H, M (unmarked), L level tones plus falling and rising contours; heavy grammatical tone (dative falling tone on prefixes, vocative tone, plural marking).

tone_statements.citation: Blench, Roger M. & Selbut R. Longtau. 2012. Tarok reduplication and syllable repetition. Draft circulated for comment, Kay Williamson Educational Foundation, Cambridge, 31 May 2012. 8 pp. (formerly at rogerblench.info, Tarok/Grammar/Tarok)
tone_statements.quote: Three level and two contour tones are noted with the mid-tone unmarked. Word order in Tarok is SAuxVO with verbs not morphologically marked for tense/aspect. [...] Although the verbs have a fixed tone in citation form, the tone becomes underspecified when they become reduplicated adjectives. In most cases such adjectives also exhibit tonal concord with the noun they qualify. [...] However, they have a distinctive tone-pattern, HH(H)LL(L) which is applied regardless of the tone of the verb.
tone_statements.summary: 3 level tones (H, M, L; M unmarked) + 2 contour tones (falling, rising); heavy grammatical use of tone (tonal concord and fixed melodies in reduplicated adjectives).

tone_statements.quote: This paper uses the phonological analysis proposed in Longtau (2008) but not the standard Tarok orthography, which has a rather misleading use of IPA symbols. … Tarok orthography does not mark tone, but there are three level tones are noted with mid-tone unmarked. Tarok also has fairly rare rising and falling tones symbolised by /ˇ/ and /ˆ/. Tarok publications mark non-phonemic labialisation of initial consonants in front of high back vowels and palatalisation before high front vowels.
tone_statements.summary: Three level tones (mid unmarked; high and low marked) plus fairly rare rising and falling tones, following Longtau 2008; datives take a falling tone on the prefix; nothing on word stress.

tone_statements.citation: Longtau, Selbut R. 2008 [2022 edited electronic edition of the 2008 volume]. The Tarok Language: Its Basic Principles and Grammar Sketch. Jos: Development Alternatives, Research & Training (DART). Print ed. xiv+241 pp. (full text as carried by the academia.edu page capture).
tone_statements.quote: Like most Nigerian languages, Tarok is tonal. There are three level tones and two contour or gliding tones. The tones are marked as follows: High (H) ´ Mid (M) marked by the absence of a tone mark Low (L) ` Falling (HF) ̂ Rising (LR) .̌ … The level tones have a very wide distribution, but the gliding ones are not only rare, but they occur mainly in grammatical contexts and in some syllable deletions. The rising tone is indeed very rare. Both kinetic tones are glides from high to mid and low to mid for the falling and rising tones respectively.
tone_statements.locator: Section 2.6 'Tonemes', pp. 34-35 (print-edition pagination per the contents list); TBU statement 2.3 p.21; floating tone 2.5.3 p.34.

tone_statements.citation: Blench, Roger M. & Selbut R. Longtau. 2012. Tarok adjectival morphology [site file 'Tarok '; = 'Tarok Adjectives 1: Morphology', cited as in press, Journal of West African Languages, in Longtau 2008]. Draft submitted to JWAL, circulation version, printout Cambridge 29 May 2012. Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. 17 pp. Formerly at rogerblench.info (Tarok/Grammar/).
tone_statements.quote: The paper uses the phonological analysis proposed in Longtau (1993) but not the standard Tarok orthography, which has a misleading use of IPA symbols. … Three level tones are noted with mid-tone unmarked. … Classes 1-4 all follow the head noun, take V or N prefixes and, with the exception of numerals, show concord with the tone on the stem of the noun they qualify. These adjectives can therefore not be marked with tone in isolation.
tone_statements.locator: 0. Introduction, p. 1 and 1.2 True adjectives, p. 3
tone_statements.summary: Three level tones (mid unmarked, high and low marked), following Longtau 1993; most adjectives copy the tone of the noun stem, insult adjectives keep a fixed tone; no more on the tone system.

tone_statements.citation: Blench, Roger M. (& Selbut R. Longtau?). n.d. Tarok verbal extensions. Working paper, rogerblench.info, Tarok/Grammar/Tarok verbal.
tone_statements.quote: The following paper1 uses the phonological analysis proposed in Longtau (1993) but not the standard Tarok orthography, which has a rather misleading use of IPA symbols. … Three level tones are noted with mid-tone unmarked. … Although sequences of dissimilar vowels occur throughout the Tarok lexicon, often associated with falling tones, suggesting that they arise from intervocalic consonant deletion, in verbs they occur only in the shape CVV.
tone_statements.locator: p. 1, sect. 1 Introduction (notation note before sect. 2) and p. 2, sect. 2 Canonical shapes of verbs
tone_statements.summary: Three level tones (mid unmarked; high and low marked), following Longtau 1993; falling tones on unlike-vowel sequences attributed to consonant loss; tone of the relic -ci suffix varies; nothing more.

tone_statements.citation: Longtau, Selbut R. n.d. [c.2013-2014; cites Storch 2012]. Morphology of derived nouns in the Tarok language of Central Nigeria (academia.edu title: 'Noun formation strategies in Tarok, Plateau State, Nigeria'). Draft chapter for a forthcoming volume on Benue-Congo languages edited by Anne Storch & Roger Blench, circulated for comment. Jos: DART. c.17 pp. academia.edu 8885528.
tone_statements.quote: There are 3 level tone melodies and 2 kinetic rising and falling ones.3 Tones are marked in this way: /´/ for a high tone mid tone is shown by an absence of a tone mark /`/ for a low tone /ˆ/ for a falling tone /ˇ/ for the rising tone. Nouns can be derived from verbs, adjectives, other nouns, adverbs, exclamations, grammatical phrases and sentences through prefixation, syllable/word apocope and tone manipulations. Tone is a major inflectional strategy in forming several singular/plural pairings and nouns with oblique tones. [...] Generally speaking, we can say the following rules seem to apply to classes 3/4: 1. High tone in all stems is retained in the plural. 2. Mid tone is raised to high. 3. Low tone is raised to mid.
tone_statements.locator: section 1 transcription conventions; noun-class section with 'Table 2 - Sample of diagnostic tone frames of simple nouns' (p.6) and plural tone rules (p.8)
tone_statements.summary: H, M, L + rising, falling; lexical and grammatical tone; plural formation by one-step tone raising on noun stems (M->H, L->M), prefix tone diagnostic of class/number.
